findings.description: The 0.1.0 release security review (docs/implementation/final-review/security-review.json) raised SEC-2 (LOW, open) and SEC-3 (INFORMATIONAL, noted). Both are characteristics the release will ship with and neither is recorded in the canonical limitations record docs/limitations.md. SEC-2 (state-root resolution falls back to Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "ArrTags") when IPluginManager is unavailable or the loaded plugin instance cannot be found) and SEC-3 (the versioned state envelope's SHA-256 covers only PayloadJson, so Terminal/UpdatedTime metadata is outside the integrity check) are accepted for V1 (both are LOW/INFORMATIONAL and not remotely reachable / not an escalation), but the release-gate condition 5 requires every accepted limitation to be recorded in docs/limitations.md. The previous audit (attempt 1) was blocked on exactly this condition for RR-1/RR-15 and was closed only by commit 6926a9a recording them; the same discipline has not been applied to SEC-2/SEC-3. This is a documentation/process gap, not a correctness defect: the release is otherwise substantively safe (artifact reproduced byte-identically, full test matrix green, full live end-to-end pipeline passes, SEC-1 fixed).
evidence: docs/implementation/final-review/security-review.json findings SEC-2 (lines 23-33) and SEC-3 (lines 35-46); reviewer_status APPROVED with no open BLOCKER/HIGH
grep of docs/limitations.md for 'temp|fallback|PluginManager|envelope|tamper|integrity hash|schema version' -> only F5 renderer fallback and ADR-008 path fallback; no SEC-2/SEC-3 entry
docs/limitations.md contains exactly the F1-F5, V1-V6, P1-P5, D1-D2, RR-1, RR-15 headings (verified each present); no SEC-* heading
.opencode/agents/orchestrator.md:717 'Verify every accepted limitation is recorded in docs/limitations.md.'
findings.recommended_action: Run a documentation-only corrective task (no code/artifact change) that records SEC-2 and SEC-3 (with user-visible consequence and evidence) in docs/limitations.md, or explicitly dispositions them there, then re-run the release review. Do not create the v0.1.0 tag before that.

findings.description: SEC-2: when IPluginManager is unavailable or the loaded plugin instance cannot be found, the authoritative plugin state root falls back to Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "ArrTags"), a predictable shared location. It is not triggered on the pinned host (Plugin is found and DataFolderPath is ProgramDataPath/ArrTags) and is not remotely reachable, so it is accepted for V1, but it must be recorded (RR-20).
evidence: live: /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags (ProgramDataPath/ArrTags) was used for all published state; no /tmp/ArrTags created
findings.recommended_action: Record as an accepted limitation (RR-20); optionally fail closed or use a host-private directory post-V1.

findings.description: SEC-3: the versioned state envelope's SHA-256 covers only PayloadJson; SchemaVersion/Kind/RecordId/Authority/Terminal/UpdatedUtc are not covered, so retention decisions trust unauthenticated Terminal/UpdatedUtc. This bounds StateEnvelopeCodec to a corruption detector rather than a tamper MAC. It is not an escalation (local write access to the state root is already the administrative boundary) and is accepted for V1, but it must be recorded (RR-20).
findings.recommended_action: Record as an accepted limitation (RR-20); optionally cover envelope metadata in the integrity hash or document the corruption-detector scope.

limitations_accepted: F1 / RR-7 - No provider inventory/catalogue cache; provider metadata is fetched per work item. Consequence: a large library performs one provider-library read per work item, so GOALS criterion 6 is only partially met for provider fetches. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F1; live unchanged re-run issued 5 provider reads while performing no render/publication.
F2 / RR-8 - Runtime configuration replacement is not wired to Jellyfin's save path. Consequence: secret/provider/badge/limit changes require a process restart. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F2.
F3 / RR-9 - No bounded metrics/diagnostic-status surface. Consequence: no supported in-product view of queue depth/provider health. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F3.

F4 / RR-10 - Reconciliation coverage is bounded by QueueCapacity. Consequence: a scope larger than 512 covers only a bounded prefix per run; event/webhook/per-item triggers unaffected. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F4.

F5 - Renderer depends on a host-supplied SkiaSharp with no bundled fallback. Consequence: a host without a compatible SkiaSharp fails closed; validated only on the pinned linux-musl-x64 Jellyfin 12.0.0 host. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F5; ADR-015; live publication.
V1 - No live Sonarr/Radarr instance. Consequence: provider payload-shape variance beyond the committed fixtures is untested. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V1; mock fixture live run.
V2 / RR-11 - ADR-010 non-canonical cross-runtime comparison unselected/unrun. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V2.
V3 / RR-12 - Jellyfin Enhanced coexistence is contract-level only. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V3.
V4 / RR-13 - Automated live SaveImage read-back absent; the live round trip is manual (this audit re-performed it). Evidence: docs/limitations.md V4.
V5 / RR-14 - Live uninstall drain: the release audit exercised it (204, install+state removed, artwork restored); automated coverage remains the in-process tests. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V5.
V6 - Host-guarded facts are skipped without the pinned host. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V6; this audit's three-suite matrix.
P1 / RR-4 - Byte-reproducibility depends on the pinned toolchain and has no automated byte-identity guard. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P1; this audit's independent reproduction.
P2 / RR-16 - Reduced debug metadata for reproducibility. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P2.
P3 - PackagePlugin=true stages but does not write the archive; ./build.sh package is the entry point. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P3.
P4 / RR-17 - SkiaSharp license notices ship although SkiaSharp is not redistributed. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P4.
P5 / RR-18 - Pre-release orphaned state/uninstall-drain retention. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P5.
D1 / RR-5 - Webhook 401 body differs from ADR-012's 'no body' text (ProblemDetails type/title/status/traceId). Evidence: docs/limitations.md D1; live 401 bodies.
D2 / RR-6 - ArtworkSubjectGate has no idle eviction. Evidence: docs/limitations.md D2.
RR-1 - Phases 1-3 lack independent phase-review records. Evidence: docs/limitations.md release-review section.
RR-15 - Documented mock fixture API keys in tracked docs. Evidence: docs/limitations.md release-review section.

SEC-2 / RR-21 - State-root resolution falls back to a shared temp path when the plugin data folder cannot be resolved. Consequence: if the fallback ever engaged, authoritative state would live under /tmp/ArrTags; not triggered on the pinned host and not remotely reachable. Evidence: src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:178-180; security-review.json SEC-2. ACCEPTED BUT NOT RECORDED IN docs/limitations.md (RR-20) - condition 5 fails.

SEC-3 / RR-22 - The state envelope integrity hash covers only PayloadJson, so StateEnvelopeCodec detects corruption but does not authenticate a malicious writer; retention trusts unauthenticated Terminal/UpdatedUtc. Consequence: none beyond the existing administrative boundary. Evidence: src/ArrTags/State/StateEnvelopeCodec.cs:83-113; security-review.json SEC-3. ACCEPTED BUT NOT RECORDED IN docs/limitations.md (RR-20) - condition 5 fails.

summary: ArrTags 0.1.0 at HEAD 75c03ab (task-stated c980b1f; the only difference is the release-review report rename) is substantively safe but the release gate is not yet passable. I independently reproduced the release artifact from a clean git-archive export of HEAD: 568,244 bytes, SHA-256 f6b6a515c76b93926e940cebd48918f864935893b2ae7d03f59b17e38e0f9ffd, 7 entries, every per-entry hash matched the recorded table, the manifest is version 0.1.0.0 / targetAbi 12.0.0.0 / framework net10.0, no SkiaSharp/HarfBuzz runtime is shipped, and the archive is cmp-equal (byte-identical) to the frozen artifacts/ArrTags_0.1.0.0.zip. The clean build reported 0 warnings / 0 errors; the default suite was 1228 passed / 60 skipped / 1288 total, the host-guarded suite 1244 / 44 / 1288, and the forced-native suite 1301 / 17 / 1318, all with 0 failed and matching the recorded post-SEC-1 baselines (the first default run without the package present was 1225/63/1288, which is the documented package-content skip). I independently exercised the full live end-to-end path on the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 musl host with the reproduced artifact: it installs and loads with exactly one 'Loaded plugin: "ArrTags" "0.1.0.0"' and 0 [FTL]; the SEC-1 fix is confirmed live (unauthenticated JSON/form/multipart all return the uniform 401 with no pre-auth body read - form 300,000 B and multipart 36.7 MB now 401 instead of the pre-fix framework 400 - authenticated JSON returns 202/400/413, authenticated non-JSON returns a bounded 400, and no secret is reflected); badges publish through the real host SaveImage path with GET bytes matching the persisted ActiveImageIdentity (85f12abb/3e267ffd, then 5134efb1 after a changed fixture); the original source artwork is byte-unchanged; unchanged metadata does not republish and changed metadata does; a provider 503 leaves the host up with artwork unchanged; restart preserves the install and all 16 state records; and an authenticated uninstall returns 204, removes the install folder and the relocated state root, and restores the served image to the original source poster. Secrets are contained (0 occurrences in logs, state, responses, or the artifact; only in Jellyfin's plugin configuration XML; no plugin logging exists; provider integration is GET-only). ADR-012 (with the SEC-1 clarification), ADR-014, ADR-015, and the data model are conformant with no drift. The one material finding is release-gate condition 5: the security review's SEC-2 (LOW, state-root temp fallback) and SEC-3 (INFORMATIONAL, envelope integrity scope) are accepted for V1 but are not recorded in docs/limitations.md, so the gate cannot pass and the tag must not be created until a documentation-only corrective task records them. All previously recorded limitations (F1-F5, V1-V6, P1-P5, D1-D2, RR-1, RR-15) remain present and accurate, and SEC-1 is resolved. Decision: DO_NOT_SHIP (CHANGES_REQUIRED) pending the documentation-only condition-5 correction.
